verdict: Both are almost the same. The difference is very small, so pick the one you like and watch how many pieces you eat.
why: Calories are almost the same: fast food original is an estimated 320 kcal, fried chicken thigh an estimated 300 kcal. Only a 20 kcal difference.
Protein is close too: 25 g vs 22 g. Both are enough to help you stay full longer.
Fat is almost identical, 20 g vs 19 g. Most of it comes from the skin and batter.
What usually pushes the calories up isn't the chicken, it's the set: sweet drink, fries and a second piece.
when_a: Fast food chicken is okay when you go out with family. Take 1 piece, plain water or a sugar-free drink, and coleslaw.
when_b: Fried chicken thigh at a warung is okay when you eat it with half a portion of rice and vegetables, not a mountain of rice with lots of gravy.
tip: Remove some of the skin and thick batter. The protein stays, and the fat drops a lot.

faq.q: Can I eat fried chicken while trying to lose weight?
faq.a: Yes. The key is 1 piece, not 3. Pair it with vegetables and a proper portion of rice. Frequency matters too, for example a few times a week, not every day.

faq.q: Which part is lower in calories, breast or thigh?
faq.a: Usually breast is lower in fat and higher in protein. But if you prefer thigh, that's fine. Controlling size and skin already makes a big difference.
